title: Test-isolation: NetworkManager host()/disconnect_from_game() poisons the shared SceneTree MultiplayerAPI for alphabetically-later GUT scripts (is_server()/get_unique_id() break for any later Player.tscn authority test)

GUT runs every tests/*.gd script in ONE shared process/SceneTree. tests/test_network_manager.gd's host()/join() tests assign a REAL ENetMultiplayerPeer to get_tree().get_multiplayer() -- the SAME root MultiplayerAPI every node in every OTHER test script also uses -- then clear it back to null on teardown. Empirically, Godot's SceneMultiplayer treats 'never had a peer' (is_server() conveniently defaults true, offline-friendly single-player default) and 'had a real peer, now cleared' (is_server() now correctly reports FALSE, get_unique_id() errors -- a real disconnected client should NOT still claim to be the server) as two DIFFERENT internal states, not the same 'offline' state. Once ANY test script assigns a real peer even once, EVERY test script that runs LATER in the same process and touches Player.tscn's is_multiplayer_authority()/get_unique_id() (CameraComponent._ready(), AbilityController._enter_tree(), etc.) inherits the 'disconnected' (not 'offline') state and fails with engine errors GUT treats as test failures. This is invisible in production (a real process only ever hosts/joins/stays offline once for its whole lifetime) and was invisible in this suite only because tests/test_ability_system.gd (the only pre-existing Player.tscn-instantiating test) happens to sort alphabetically BEFORE test_network_manager.gd -- not because it was actually safe; test_role_state_machine.gd sorts AFTER it and was the first to surface this. title: [S2] Start-Match readiness-barrier grace-timer (8s) force-disconnects a legit unfocused client -- recurring, blocks team 2-instance testing
human_pass_result: PASS (2026-07-19, human 2-instance). Client alt-tabbed/backgrounded during Start Match was NOT force-disconnected; both windows landed in the arena with both Players present, no origin-stack/desync. Producer closes TK-P2-30.

fix_note: network-engineer, 2026-07-18. ROOT CAUSE (identified + documented, not guessed): an occluded/backgrounded OS window's frame loop is throttled hard by the OS compositor + vsync (down to a handful of fps while occluded). Godot drives BOTH scene-load completion (deferred change_scene_to_file -> TestArena instancing -> PlayerSpawner._ready()) AND the multiplayer poll/flush that actually SENDS the queued reliable _rpc_arena_ready packet from that same main loop -- so a healthy-but-backgrounded client's readiness legitimately lands well past the 8s ARENA_READY_GRACE_SEC, and the old grace timer force-disconnected it as if crashed. Confirmed this is stock engine+OS behavior, NOT a project misconfig: project.godot sets no low_processor_usage_mode / max_fps / vsync override (all Godot defaults). FIX (server-side, host stays fully authoritative -- evaluated all 3 human-suggested directions): chose (b) + a defensible reframing of (a); REJECTED (a)-alone (a blind bigger timeout is indefensible -- an occluded window can throttle arbitrarily long, no fixed number is safe) and did NOT apply (c) here (forcing a backgrounded window to keep rendering/flushing is a rendering/perf-domain change with side effects, and the broader 'backgrounded client in a LIVE match also stops replicating' problem is bigger than this barrier -- flagged for TK-P2-20 / architect, see below). Implementation: at each grace elapse, a still-unready peer that is STILL CONNECTED at the ENet layer (in NetworkManager.get_connected_peer_ids()) is proven alive, so the host EXTENDS the grace (keeps the whole barrier held -- still never spawns toward an absent peer, zero new path-cache-poison risk) instead of killing it, up to ARENA_READY_MAX_GRACE_EXTENSIONS (new const=3 -> worst-case hold 8s*(1+3)=32s). Only a peer truly gone from the transport, or one that burns the whole extension budget while still connected (genuinely wedged), reaches the ORIGINAL TK-P2-13 force-disconnect-then-spawn fallback -- so one hung peer still can never deadlock the match forever (deadlock protection preserved, just evidence-gated and bounded at 32s instead of a hair-trigger 8s kill). Decision logic extracted to pure static networking/ArenaBarrierRules.decide_grace_action() (same pure-helper/thin-shell split as RoundRules/StaggerRules/SafeCircleRules). Also stopped the grace Timer on normal barrier release (resolves the TK-P2-22 'stop grace timer' nit) and reused a single Timer node across extensions (no per-extension node leak). FILES: networking/PlayerSpawner.gd (grace-timeout logic + consts + timer reuse/stop), networking/ArenaBarrierRules.gd (NEW pure logic), tests/test_arena_barrier_rules.gd (NEW, 11 GUT cases incl. max-extensions=0 -> original-behavior boundary), tests/net/spawn_probe_slowjoin_peer.gd + tests/net/run_spawn_probe_slowjoin.sh (NEW B2-pattern headless probe).
